sentences.text: Heat pump, or furnace plus air conditioning? One study's median installed costs came out $270 apart.

resolved.explanation: The sentence speaks $6,185 as what it costs to install a heat pump, with no date on the money. The study's own methods line says the installation costs come from the National Residential Efficiency Measures Database 'adjusted to $2020 USD', a national average at one assumed capacity (36,000 BTU/hr). In a Short nothing else corrects it, and a viewer holding a 2026 quote against a bare $6,185 would conclude they are being overcharged by a wide margin: the package's own premise cites a $15,900 median in one 2021-2024 programme and a $6,600 to $29,000 national range. 'Not quotes' tells the viewer the figure is not a contractor's price; it does not tell them the figure is six years old. The $270 gap and the 80 percent overlap are unaffected (both sides are in the same dollars), so only the absolute figure needs the date.
resolved.suggestion: Date the money beside the figure: '$6,185 in 2020 dollars to install the heat pump, with the furnace-and-air-conditioning median just above it'. Three words, and the runtime stays under 50 seconds.
